pr.title: Show packed field alignment in mir_transform_unaligned_packed_ref
pr.description:
Fixes rust-lang/rust#147528

I left the expected padding for the field out of the error message so the message would be the same on all platforms. It also isn't always possible to know the expected alignment, so this makes the message simpler.
pr.author: 21aslade

issues.title: Confusing error message with unaligned access to `packed(n > 1)` fields
issues.body:
### Code

```Rust
#[repr(C, packed(4))]
pub struct Data {
    oxide_magic: u32,
    header_version: u32,
    monotonic_counter: u64,
    slot_select: u32,
}

fn main() {
    let d = Data {
        oxide_magic: 1,
        header_version: 1,
        monotonic_counter: 4,
        slot_select: 15,
    };
    println!("{}", d.monotonic_counter);
}
```

### Current output

```Shell
error[E0793]: reference to packed field is unaligned
  --> src/main.rs:16:20
   |
16 |     println!("{}", d.monotonic_counter);
   |                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: packed structs are only aligned by one byte, and many modern architectures penalize unaligned field accesses
   = note: creating a misaligned reference is undefined behavior (even if that reference is never dereferenced)
   = help: copy the field contents to a local variable, or replace the reference with a raw pointer and use `read_unaligned`/`write_unaligned` (loads and stores via `*p` must be properly aligned even when using raw pointers)
   = note: this error originates in the macro `$crate::format_args_nl` which comes from the expansion of the macro `println` (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0793`.
error: could not compile `playground` (bin "playground") due to 1 previous er
```

### Desired output
Something along the lines of
```Shell
   = note: this struct is aligned to 4 bytes, but the variable requires 8-byte alignment
   = note: many modern architectures penalize unaligned field accesses
   = ...etc
```

### Rationale and extra context

It's confusing to see `packed structs are only aligned by one byte` when I have specified `packed(4)`

### Rust Version

```Shell
rustc 1.90.0 (1159e78c4 2025-09-14)
binary: rustc
commit-hash: 1159e78c4747b02ef996e55082b704c09b970588
commit-date: 2025-09-14
host: aarch64-apple-darwin
release: 1.90.0
LLVM version: 20.1.8
```

processing.reason: The PR is a diagnostic-only refactor; there is no source-grounded runtime/MIR value transformation to encode. The diff changes `is_disaligned`/`is_within_packed` into `place_unalignment`/`most_packed_projection`, but every listed consumer only tests Option presence: AddMovesForPackedDrops uses `.is_some()`, DeadStoreElimination and Validator use `.is_none()`/`.is_some()`, and CheckPackedRef still errors under the same condition. The new helper computes the same minimum packed alignment (`min_by_key` over the same pack values) and the same bool via `place_unalignment(...).is_some() == is_disaligned(...)`. The only observable change is the E0793 error/note text: it now reports `adt.descr()` and `pack.bytes()` instead of hard-coding a one-byte packed struct. That diagnostic cannot be observed by running a program: any `&packed_field` triggering CheckPackedRef is a compile error (E0793), so it cannot be executed under Miri, and `test_program_pair` compares runtime return values rather than stderr. Fabricating a function that returns the rendered note value (e.g. alignment 1 vs N) would merely re-encode the diagnostic string, not model an actual historical wrong MIR/program transformation, and would violate the instruction to hold borrow/MIR behavior constant and compare the diagnostic instead of generated code. Therefore no legitimate original/transformed Rust pair with differing runtime values can be validated from this PR.

analysis.summary: This PR fixes the E0793 diagnostic for borrows of fields inside `#[repr(packed(N))]` types. The old diagnostic helper discarded both the actual packed alignment and the kind of ADT, so a `packed(4)` struct was described as a one-byte-packed struct and packed unions were called structs. The refactor makes the packed-place helper return the `AdtDef` and minimum packed `Align`, allowing CheckPackedRef to emit the real type kind and alignment. AddMovesForPackedDrops, DeadStoreElimination, and Validator only consume the helper as an `Option` (`is_some`/`is_none`), so their MIR optimization/validation behavior is unchanged; this is a diagnostic bug fix, not an optimization semantic rewrite.
analysis.originalLogic: `is_disaligned` returned a plain `bool`, and `is_within_packed` returned only `Option<Align>` computed as the minimum `repr().pack` among packed base ADTs before the first `Deref`. CheckPackedRef then emitted `UnalignedPackedRef { span }`, whose message template said "reference to packed field is unaligned" and whose note always claimed "packed structs are only aligned by one byte, and many modern architectures penalize unaligned field accesses". Thus the underlying ADT identity and actual packed alignment were available during analysis but thrown away before rendering.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For every place judged unaligned, the old diagnostic rendering transformed the underlying packed fact into a fixed one-byte-struct explanation. It did so even when the containing ADT was `#[repr(packed(4))]` (or another `packed(N)` with N > 1) or was a union; it also lost which nested ADT supplied the minimum pack. This is a diagnostic-rendering transformation, not a program/MIR rewrite: old `is_disaligned(...)` and new `place_unalignment(...).is_some()` agree, and old `is_within_packed(...).is_some()` and new `most_packed_projection(...).is_some()` agree. A two-program pair should hold the borrow/MIR behavior constant and vary only the packed container (`packed(1)` vs `packed(4)`/union), then compare the diagnostic, not generated code.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR places with projections from ADTs carrying `repr(packed(N))`, N >= 1, including plain packed structs, packed unions, nested packed ADTs, fields with dyn/unsized or slice/str tails, and places used in borrow contexts (CheckPackedRef), `Drop` terminators (AddMovesForPackedDrops), call destinations and `Operand::Move` arguments (DeadStoreElimination and Validator).
analysis.trigger: CheckPackedRef visits a borrow of a field whose place lies within a packed ADT and whose field type may require alignment greater than the packed alignment, especially when pack is 2/4/8 or the ADT is a union. The bug is visible in the emitted E0793 note, not necessarily in whether the borrow is rejected.
preconditions: Walk `place.projection` only up to the first `ProjectionElem::Deref`; a Deref stops the packed scan because the pointee is no longer a direct packed projection.
For each base, require `base.ty(...).ty.ty_adt_def()` and `adt.repr().pack`; only such bases contribute a packed alignment.
Choose the projection with the lowest pack via `min_by_key(|(_, align)| *align)`, and return the `AdtDef` associated with that minimum, not an arbitrary packed ADT.
If the field layout is known and its alignment is <= the packed alignment, do not report unalignment; unsized tails are exceptions, but slice/str tails have known alignments.
If layout cannot be determined, conservatively treat the place as unaligned and return the packed ADT/align.
CheckPackedRef emits the error only for borrow contexts; builtin derive creating an unaligned reference is still a compiler bug.
pitfalls: Do not hard-code the note to one-byte packing: `repr(packed(4))` must say 4-byte aligned, and `packed(2)` must say 2-byte aligned.
Do not call every packed ADT a struct: use `adt.descr()` so packed unions report "packed union".
The FTL note must omit "at most " only for alignment 1 and include it for larger packed alignments.
Preserve the association between the minimum pack and its ADT; nested packed structs can have different ADTs and alignments.
Do not scan through `Deref`: fields behind pointers are not direct packed-field borrows.
Do not assume all packed places are rejected: a field whose type alignment is <= pack is allowed, e.g. align-2 or align-1 fields in a packed(2) type.
This PR does not change AddMovesForPackedDrops, DeadStoreElimination, or Validator decisions; expecting different MIR optimization output is a misreading of the refactor.
analysis.testStrategy: Use compile-fail UI tests that differ only in the packed container: `#[repr(packed)]` (1-byte), `#[repr(packed(2))]`, `#[repr(packed(4))]`, and a packed union, all borrowing a field that requires greater alignment. Assert exact `.stderr` text, including `reference to field of packed struct/union is unaligned`, `this struct/union is [at most ]N-byte aligned`, and absence of the old universal one-byte claim. Add nested-packed cases to verify the minimum pack and its ADT are reported, dyn-trait versus slice-tail cases to exercise conservative layout handling, and negative cases where the field alignment is <= pack. Keep raw-pointer-immediate borrow tests because CheckPackedRef still rejects them. Update expected stderr alongside the `.rs` annotations; no compiler was built or executed here.
